title: The Thanksgiving Turkey
seo_title: Thanksgiving Turkey Charcuterie Board: Showpiece Plan & List
description: A Thanksgiving turkey charcuterie board for 12 to 15: a turkey with a fanned tail of salami, prosciutto, smoked turkey, cheddar triangles, Gouda and apples.
hook: A turkey with a tail full of everyone's favorite foods.
why: The body is one ordinary thing from the produce aisle, so the turkey takes minutes. The tail is the board: fanned rows of soppressata, prosciutto, smoked turkey, cheddar triangles, Gouda cubes and apple slices.
It's rated 2 of 5, one of the easiest showpieces, and it's the appetizer kids will want to help with.

timeline.what: Seed the pomegranates (or buy the seeds), slice the cheddar into triangles, and cube the Gouda and white cheddar.
Slice the apples and toss them in lemon water to keep them white.
Build the turkey head, then the feathers, then the pomegranate band and the outer border.
Add the rosemary between the feathers.

faq.q: How do you make a turkey charcuterie board?
faq.a: Build a fan-shaped tail of meat, cheese and fruit rows, then add the turkey's body and face at the front. The book shows the one produce-aisle trick for the body.

faq.q: How much should I make before Thanksgiving dinner?
faq.a: As an appetizer before the meal, plan about 1½ to 2 oz each of meat and cheese per guest.

Cut the cheese and fan the meats the day before. Slice the apples last and toss them in lemon juice. Keep meat, cheese and cut fruit out no more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. For a long party, build half, keep the refill in the fridge and top it up halfway through.
